review: Static source/module inventory; not runtime validation or automated tests

files.purpose: A validated aim hint for this cast only. Projectiles still collide normally; there is no homing, automatic attack or direct damage to the chosen target.
Exploration equipment: modest passive bonuses and deliberate, paid right-click actions.
Cosmetic focus. It never changes existing class weapons or their combat values.
Permanent point allocation. One point per level gained, independently of skill points.
Stable UUID-seeded layout. Old allocations remain bonuses outside this new graph.
Class-bound variants of native items. Receipt and pending inventory share the player's saved NBT.
Three permanent lessons per class; reward and completion share one atomic profession record.
A registered class artifact activates through the game's configurable Use Item binding.
Soulbound equipment recovery uses saved player NBT, not a session-only item cache.
Discoverable descriptions, never grants items or changes the player's inventory.
Read-only inventory comparison. Nothing is equipped, spent or transferred by this screen.
Optional client bridge: the flight controller owns view rotation while active.
Opt-in client integration fixture; only runs in a dedicated dev directory and named QA world.
Numerical rules independent of Minecraft, shared by runtime and regression tests.
Projects markers through the world projection, including damage and FOV effects.
Class identity with an embedded owo component selector and native detail cards.
Read-only comparison uses the same slot and modifier operations as equipment.
Two tooltips while the configured comparison key is held, without changing inventory input.
Camera-relative compass and debounced region transitions; no server packets or chunk loads.
Advancement-style canvas with pointer-anchored zoom and drag-to-pan.
Opacity is captured when GUI commands are queued, including deferred item icons.
Poll the player's mapped movement bindings, never fixed WASD codes.
Normalized placement stays inside the viewport when resolution/GUI scale changes.
Quest journal: objectives, progress and reward are presented on a readable page.
Separate the visible character's facing from camera/interaction aim. Vanilla WASD remains camera-relative and the server keeps the ordinary interaction direction.
Declare every present and future shortcut through this factory; registration is automatic.
Navigation hub; skills are used through the configured gameplay keys.
Shared RPG slider appearance, preserving native pointer and keyboard handling.
Shared original RPG frames built from vanilla items and GUI primitives.
Stable player orientation, with a projected reticle instead of frame-dependent toe-in.
Loaded terrain and cave floors, bounded sampling and one uploaded terrain texture.
Short depth-occluded impact waves; bounded and cleared on world changes.
Original vector pictograms; consistent strokes at every GUI scale.
Look assistance uses ordinary rotation packets, without bypassing server reach.
Wall-clock easing stays smooth when the integrated world is paused.
Nine-slice of vanilla inventory frame, with a blank center rather than stretched slots.
Ground contours projected with the world camera; walls occlude each segment.
One server roll per direct hit, before armor, shield durability or health are spent.
Feedback comes from completed server damage, never from a client damage estimate.
Short telegraphs, line-of-sight attacks and bounded native enemy reinforcements.
One persistent secondary identity per elite, plus a low-health combat phase.
Pure client preview plus authoritative slot guard; never creates, deletes or moves stacks.
Drained water is restored; a durable ledger also recovers pockets after a restart.
Vanilla drinking consumes one bottle; the server restores the real mana pool.
Large impacts are processed over several ticks, with a global block/entity budget.
Covers target acquisition as well as goals that validate targets without a change event.
Level is assigned once, after vanilla spawn setup, and saved with the mob.
Level gates quality; luck increases the roll chance without bypassing those gates.
Separate world/UUID record: class resets do not destroy profession or villager progress.
One file per UUID, inside each world; never replaces unreadable profiles with defaults.
Stable recurring contracts; exact entity ids keep objectives unambiguous.
Small server-owned patrols in loaded outdoor terrain, separated from village raids.
Server-authoritative skills using vanilla entities, items, effects, particles and sounds.
Server owns duration, costs and impacts; the local player simulates the same glide as vanilla.
Authoritative settings are SERVER configs, synchronized by NeoForge.
Atomic, validated datapack definitions. Stable node IDs and objective sizes preserve old saves.
Generates class definitions, quest definitions, recipe, data maps and the developer test template.
Session-only skill overrides. Real points, class and cooldown are never overwritten.
Server-owned charges. Test mode spends charges normally; only debug bypasses them.
Session-owned vanilla creatures. No permanent blocks, pets, loot or spawn-level modifications.
Immutable progression: RPG experience is independent of vanilla experience.
Native profiler sections plus optional local timing counters; no telemetry or uploads.
Vanilla visual lightning and splash potions, with authoritative hand/mana/timer checks.
Bounded, server-owned casts. Temporary creatures never produce loot or XP.
Cosmetic messages never alter damage, targeting, resources or terrain.
Versioned three-branch tree: preparation, minor effect, minor upgrade, main, two upgrades, capstone.
Class silhouettes affect coordinates only; node IDs and unlock dependencies stay intact.
Only places in air. Durable expiry ledger prevents temporary blocks surviving a restart.
Reduces only unopened vanilla village chest loot; other structures and inventories are untouched.
